pageIntro.title: A nonprofit movement helping children see technology as something they can shape.
pageIntro.description: Free Code Juniors combines accessible teaching, creative project work, and community support so students do not just learn coding concepts, they build belief in their own potential.

mission.title: Our Mission
mission.description: To make computer science education accessible to every child through thoughtful instruction, creative learning experiences, and a nonprofit model centered on inclusion and encouragement.

vision.title: Our Vision
vision.description: A future where every young learner, regardless of background or experience, has the opportunity to become an innovator, engineer, builder, and problem-solver.

whyCoding.title: Why coding matters
paragraphs: Coding gives students more than a technical skill. It teaches logic, persistence, collaboration, and the habit of turning ideas into something real.
When children build games, stories, apps, and prototypes, they discover that technology is not just something they consume. It is something they can create with purpose and imagination.
Those early experiences matter. They help young people see themselves as capable problem-solvers long before they make choices about school, college, or career paths.

whyNonprofit.title: Why Nonprofit education matters to us
paragraphs: A nonprofit model keeps the focus where it belongs: access, community impact, and meaningful student growth.
It allows Free Code Juniors to invest in welcoming learning spaces, volunteer mentorship, and accessible teaching practices instead of optimizing for exclusivity.
That mission-first approach makes it easier to meet families where they are and open doors for more students to participate with confidence.

team.title: Leadership
team.description: Free Code Juniors is led by co-founders who shape the curriculum, teach students, and help grow a welcoming instructor community.

members.name: Andrew Chen
members.bio:
Andrew Chen is the Co-Founder of Free Code Juniors and a passionate programmer and robotics enthusiast. He is especially interested in machine learning and applying AI to science research. Andrew has participated in FIRST LEGO League (FLL) and earned recognition in state competitions.

Through Free Code Juniors, Andrew helps create fun, hands-on programming experiences for all ages by creating the core Python and Scratch content. He is committed to giving back to the community and inspiring kids to discover the joy of coding.

Andrew also plays violin and enjoys sharing his love of music through community performances.

members.name: Zibo Nie
members.bio:
Zibo is passionate about coding, robotics, and technology. As the Co-Founder of a youth coding initiative, he is committed to giving back to the community by providing free programming experiences and helping younger students discover the joy of coding.

He has experience with Python, FTC, and VEX Robotics and has edited and organized the Python course curriculum and teaching materials used in the program. He enjoys building projects, solving problems, and helping younger students learn through hands-on coding.

Beyond technology, Zibo is a violist in the FYO Symphony Orchestra and enjoys playing tennis.

instructors.name: Leonardo Carvalho
instructors.profileRole: Director of Online Programs & Curriculum | Teaching Instructor
instructors.bio:
Leonardo "Leo" Carvalho is a high school student passionate about computer science, AI, robotics, and bioengineering. He has been coding from a young age, with experience in Java and Python, and has participated in robotics since fifth grade.

His recent projects include designing and simulating an AI-assisted knee exoskeleton for ACL rehabilitation, combining machine learning with robotic control.

As Director of Online Programs & Curriculum, Leo develops course materials and hands-on coding projects, leads virtual classes, and mentors younger students.

Outside of technology, Leo is the founder of OCAPEX, a student-led community service organization.

instructors.name: Adriano Carvalho
instructors.bio:
Adriano Carvalho is a 15-year-old sophomore. He is passionate about technology, coding, and using his creativity to help younger students discover new skills. He enjoys collaborating with others and participating in student-led community initiatives.

Beyond technology, Adriano serves as Principal Cellist of both the Florida Youth Orchestra (FYO) Symphony Orchestra and his school orchestra. He also enjoys composing music, playing piano, ice hockey, and flying airplanes.

instructors.name: Leon Rao
instructors.bio:
Leon has a strong interest in programming and robotics. He has participated in competitive robotics at multiple levels, including FIRST LEGO League (FLL), VEX IQ, FIRST Tech Challenge (FTC), and currently FIRST Robotics Competition (FRC).

Through his hands-on experience in robotics, Leon has developed and strengthened his programming skills in Python and Java, applying what he learns beyond the classroom to real-world, goal-driven challenges. He especially enjoys the problem-solving, teamwork, and creativity involved in designing and programming robots.

Leon is excited to share his knowledge and enthusiasm with younger students and hopes to help them discover how fun and rewarding programming and robotics can be.

Outside of robotics, Leon plays euphonium and trombone in concert and jazz bands. He is also an enthusiastic video gamer.

instructors.name: Christina Koyama
instructors.bio:
Christina Koyama attends American Heritage School in Delray Beach. She is a member of the school's Mu Alpha Theta math team and enjoys participating in mathematics competitions. She also volunteers as a math tutor at American Heritage, helping fellow students with math.

Christina has completed Python programming training through X-Camp, where she developed an interest in coding and problem-solving. In her free time, she enjoys music and plays both the piano and flute. She has had the opportunity to participate in many local and international music competitions, which have been valuable learning and rewarding experiences.

Most of all, Christina enjoys learning new things, meeting new people, and making friends along the way. She looks forward to exploring new opportunities and continuing to grow both academically and personally.

instructors.name: Andres Silverio
instructors.bio:
Andres Silverio is a 14-year-old ninth-grade student attending FAU High School in 2026. He has been passionate about coding since the age of five and has spent years developing his skills to solve problems through programming.

Now, Andres hopes to help other students begin their own coding journeys. As a Scratch instructor at Free Code Juniors, he helps young learners discover their potential and pursue their interests in computer programming.

Andres breaks down complex concepts into manageable steps, teaching students to apply logical thinking through basic rules, hands-on examples, and experimentation. By combining small building blocks of code, sprites, and creative ideas, he guides students in transforming simple concepts into complete projects and shows how individual pieces can come together to create something meaningful.

teacherAssistants.name: Enjun Kang
teacherAssistants.bio:
Enjun attends American Heritage School and enjoys community service and public speaking. She has hosted the 2026 Overseas Chinese Spring Festival Gala and serves as a volunteer emcee for music performances at local senior living communities.

Outside of volunteering, Enjun enjoys swimming, cheerleading, and horseback riding.

teacherAssistants.name: Jacob Spector
teacherAssistants.bio:
Jacob Spector is a 7th-grade student at American Heritage School in Plantation, Florida, with a strong interest in problem-solving, technology, and leadership. He uses his knowledge and skills to tackle complex challenges and now hopes to help other students on their own learning journeys.

Jacob enjoys helping young learners realize their potential in mathematics from the basics up. He breaks down complex problems into digestible steps so students can understand foundational rules, apply logic with confidence, and build stronger problem-solving skills.
